**RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination**
**Reference Number: POC-EE22487639-86426**
**Member: Jordan Foster / Member ID: W794852405**
**Procedure: CPT 63030 (posterior lumbar decompression/discectomy)**
**Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-07**

To the Appeals Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-07 (reference POC-EE22487639-86426). This appeal is submitted within the 180-calendar-day window stated in that notice (deadline 2027-02-03).

**Stated reason for denial**

The notice states: "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery."

**Policy the plan applies**

Based on my own research, Ambetter of North Carolina Inc. lists an active clinical policy titled "Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures," Reference Number CP.MP.114, on its public Clinical Payment Policies page as the medical-necessity document governing disc decompression/discectomy procedures. The copy of that policy I was able to retrieve (Date of Last Revision: 04/25) states, in relevant part:

"It is the policy of health plans affiliated with Centene Corporation® that open discectomy and microdiscectomy are medically necessary when meeting all of the following: A. Age ≥ 18 years; B. Diagnosis of herniated lumbar disc; C. Nerve root compression confirmed by imaging and one of the following: ... 2. Radiculopathy with sensory deficit as evidenced by pain, parasthesias or numbness in a nerve root distribution, and member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative therapy including all the following: a. ≥ four weeks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee's inability to tolerate; b. ≥ four weeks activity modification; c. One of the following: i. NSAID or acetaminophen ≥ three weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated; ii. Epidural steroid injection."

I was not able to confirm with certainty that this 04/25-dated copy is the exact version in effect on the date of my denial, and I have found a separate, older copy of the same policy number containing a six-week (rather than four-week) physical-therapy/activity-modification threshold. I am not attributing any language to the plan beyond what is quoted above, and I respectfully ask the Appeals Department to identify, in writing, the specific version and section of CP.MP.114 (or any other criteria) actually applied to my request, so that I can confirm this analysis or supplement the record accordingly.

**How the clinical record satisfies the quoted criteria**

1. **Age ≥ 18 years:** [Patient date of birth to be confirmed from chart] — I am an adult member, satisfying this element.

2. **Diagnosis of herniated lumbar disc; nerve root compression confirmed by imaging:** MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-06-28 documents an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This directly satisfies both the "diagnosis of herniated lumbar disc" and "nerve root compression confirmed by imaging" elements.

3. **Radiculopathy with sensory deficit in a nerve root distribution:** Clinical exam documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged L4-L5/L5 level, with radicular pain extending into the right calf. This corresponds to the sensory/radicular findings described in the quoted criterion. [If the reviewer requires an explicit graded motor-strength (Medical Research Council 0–5) finding under the motor-deficit pathway of the same policy, I am requesting that Dr. Reyes submit an addendum documenting that grade, as it may not be separately itemized in the records already submitted.]

4. **Failed conservative therapy — physical therapy:** I completed 16 visits of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, over 10 weeks (2026-05-03 through 2026-07-12), as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This meets and exceeds the "≥ four weeks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program" element quoted above.

5. **Failed conservative therapy — medication:** I used NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, which meets and substantially exceeds the "NSAID or acetaminophen ≥ three weeks" element quoted above.

6. **Failed conservative therapy — injection option:** I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-09 that provided only 3 weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned. [Please confirm whether this injection is documented in the chart as an epidural steroid injection specifically, as the quoted criterion lists "Epidural steroid injection" as one qualifying option; if the injection type is not already specified in the operative/procedure note, I will obtain that clarification from the administering physician.]

7. **Activity modification:** The records document that I am functionally unable to stand for more than 10 minutes due to pain, which has necessarily limited my activity for the 12-month symptom duration. [The submitted records do not appear to contain a separate, explicitly labeled "activity modification" instruction or note; I am requesting that this be added by way of a supplemental physician statement, since the functional limitation itself has been continuous and directly caused by the L4-L5 pathology at issue.]

8. **Duration and progression:** Symptoms have been present and progressive for 12 months, unrelieved by rest, which is well beyond any conservative-care window referenced in the quoted policy language, and supports that further conservative management is unlikely to be effective.

9. **No contraindications to surgery:** The record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoker status, none of which the quoted policy identifies as a bar to surgery.

**Conclusion**

Based on the imaging, examination findings, and the documented 10-week/16-visit physical therapy course, 6-month NSAID trial, and corticosteroid injection described above, I respectfully submit that the record — taken together — reflects the "adequate trial of conservative treatment" contemplated by the plan's own quoted criteria, and that CPT 63030 should be approved. To the extent the plan believes any specific sub-element (graded motor strength, injection type, or a separately documented "activity modification" instruction) is still missing, I ask that this be identified specifically so that Dr. Reyes's office can supply a short supplemental addendum rather than a full re-review.

I am requesting reconsideration and reversal of the denial. Please also send me, in writing, a copy of the exact clinical criteria document (including version/date) that was applied to my prior authorization request, as I am entitled to receive this under my plan.

Enclosed/attached with this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-03 to 2026-07-12, 16 visits)
- MRI lumbar spine report dated 2026-06-28
- Clinic notes documenting NSAID trial and corticosteroid injection (2026-06-09)
- Surgeon's (Dr. Reyes) clinical notes and exam findings
- [Any additional supporting documentation, including physician addendum(s), if obtained]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the applicable timeframe for review. If my treating physician believes that delay in resolving this appeal could seriously jeopardize my health or ability to regain function, I ask that this be treated as an expedited appeal, and I will ask Dr. Reyes's office to submit a supporting statement to that effect.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Jordan Foster
